notes:
SUMMARY OF FOUR edit_test_run CALLS MADE (all 200, all against TR-9110 / 17577900 / project 379335744):
1) body={run_state:'new_run', test_case_ids:[1985019,1985020]} -> test_cases_count went 3 -> 2. Re-read via get_test_cases_for_v1_test_run confirmed only TC-54486 (mapping 2150424053) and TC-54485 (mapping 2150424052) remained; TC-54455/54456/54458 were SILENTLY DETACHED.
2) Recovery: body={run_state:'new_run', test_case_ids:[1971631,1971632,1975349,1985019,1985020]} (all 3 original + 2 new) -> test_cases_count went to 5, and a re-read confirmed all 5 present with NEW mapping_ids for the three re-added cases (TC-54455 mapping 2150424057, TC-54456 mapping 2150424056, TC-54458 mapping 2150424058 - all changed from their pre-detachment values, proof these are fresh mappings, not the originals reattached). This same response ALSO showed owner going from 3741 to null, despite owner never being sent.
3) Owner-restore attempt: body={run_state:'new_run', owner:3741}. The response itself echoed owner:null and an unchanged updated_at (STALE - matches the systemic write-misreporting pattern already documented in findings/test-run-writes-untrustworthy-systemic.md for update_test_run_v2/replace_test_run_v2, now reproduced on edit_test_run/v1 too). An independent re-read one call later showed owner:3741 with a fresh updated_at - the write DID apply, the response body just didn't reflect it.
4) PUT-vs-PATCH probe requested by the task: body={run_state:'new_run', name:'__mcp-probe-createrun-20260921-name-edit-probe'} - no owner, no test_case_ids. Re-reads (two independent capabilities: get_test_run_cases_v1 and get_test_cases_for_v1_test_run) confirmed: (a) the 5 cases from step 2 were UNTOUCHED (still 5, same mapping_ids) - so PATCH-style partial-field semantics hold for the CASE LIST when the case-selection keys are omitted entirely; (b) owner was cleared to null AGAIN, the second reproduction, this time by a call that never mentioned test_case_ids at all - proving the owner-clearing is not test_case_ids-specific, it happens on ANY edit_test_run call that omits owner. Owner was restored a final time afterward (call 5, not counted above since it repeats call 3's shape) and independently verified durable at owner:3741 with test_cases_count:5.

FINDING 1 (CRITICAL, contradicts declared contract, data-loss hazard): test_case_ids is documented ('This is additive for cases: test_case_ids and selection ADD to the run and never remove') but behaves as a full REPLACE of the run's case list with exactly the ids sent. Confirmed twice: sending [1985019,1985020] alone dropped the run from 3 cases to exactly those 2; sending all 5 ids together produced exactly 5. Any caller trusting the documented additive semantics and sending only new case ids to 'add a case to a run' will silently detach every other case already in it - this is precisely the misreading that made bulk_assign_test_cases_to_test_run look like the wrong tool for the job in the first place, and edit_test_run's own docs actively mislead toward the same mistake. ANSWER TO THE TASK'S QUESTION: TR-9110 ended up with 5 cases only after explicitly resending all 5 ids in one call - not because test_case_ids merged with the existing selection.

FINDING 2 (CRITICAL, product/data-integrity bug, reproduced twice): owner is cleared to null by ANY edit_test_run call that omits the owner field, even one touching only name and run_state. This contradicts the omit-to-preserve semantics implied for every other optional field (tags, is_dynamic, configurations, etc., all documented 'omit the key to leave alone'). This was reproduced twice independently (once alongside a test_case_ids edit, once with an edit touching only name), each time confirmed via two different read capabilities (get_test_run_by_integer_id_v1 and get_test_run_cases_v1) taken after the stale write-response had already been observed to lag. The task assumed owner would be 'verified durable through two independent readers' across a name-only edit - it is NOT durable; it must be resent on every single edit_test_run call or the run loses its owner.

FINDING 3 (write response staleness, extends existing systemic finding): edit_test_run's write response can echo pre-write field values for fields the caller did not send in that call (observed for owner and updated_at, exactly as findings/test-run-writes-untrustworthy-systemic.md documented for update_test_run_v2 and replace_test_run_v2). This is the same failure mode reproduced on a third, v1, endpoint - widening that finding's scope beyond the v2 routes it was previously confirmed on. Fields the caller DID send in the same call (name, test_case_ids) were reflected correctly and immediately.

FINDING 4 (three-field serializer check requested by the task): is_dynamic (boolean) and overall_progress (non-null object) are CORRECT on every edit response, matching create_test_run_v1's already-confirmed-correct behavior. project_id is WRONG - returned as an integer despite being declared a string on this exact endpoint's own schema. This means the project_id defect is NOT isolated to get_test_runs_v1's list serializer alone (as the create-side probe hypothesized) - edit_test_run's write-response serializer shares it. The clean 'write path is right, one reader is broken' conclusion does not hold; project_id is wrong on at least two paths (list read, edit write) and right on at least one (create write).

FINDING 5 (minor, contrasts with create): type and self_ui_link remain declared-but-never-returned on edit too (consistent with create_test_run_v1's finding - looks like a dead field across the whole test_run surface, not isolated). observability_url and the top-level skipped_test_case_ids key, by contrast, ARE present and correct on every edit response, unlike create_test_run_v1 where both are declared-but-absent - so edit's serializer keeps two promises that create's serializer breaks for the identical entity.

RESULT FOR THE TASK'S UNBLOCKING GOAL: TC-54485 (1985019) -> mapping_id 2150424052. TC-54486 (1985020) -> mapping_id 2150424053. TR-9110 ends the probe holding all 5 cases (TC-54455/56/58/85/86), owner 3741, run_state new_run, active_state active, NOT closed, name changed to '__mcp-probe-createrun-20260921-name-edit-probe' (as part of the requested PATCH-vs-PUT name-only test - left renamed, not reverted, since nothing asked for reversion and it remains an obviously-a-probe name). TR-9075, TR-9061, TR-9062 and TR-9111 were never referenced or touched by any call in this probe.
